title: John Chrysostom (c. 347–407)
hookLine: the golden-mouthed preacher: honor Christ in the poor before you gild his altar

cards: Silk hangings. Gold cups on the altar. And outside, someone with no clothes, in the cold.

Those pictures sit side by side in one of John's sermons on Matthew, and he puts them there to make his listeners uncomfortable. Tradition remembers him by a nickname, Chrysostom, golden-mouthed, for his preaching.
But the golden mouth wasn't always sweet. He asks his wealthy listeners where they keep their gold, and who they think they're honoring with it.

teach.h: DO YOU WANT TO HONOR HIS BODY?
teach.b: First, the question, from one of his sermons on Matthew. Do you want to honor the body of Christ? Then don't ignore him when he is naked.
Don't honor him here in church with silk, while outside you neglect him, cold and without clothes.
Second, why he can say that. He's leaning on Jesus's own words in Matthew, the same words Sulpicius tied to Martin's cloak.
In the Douay-Rheims: "Amen I say to you, as long as you did it to one of these my least brethren, you did it to me."

Chrysostom points out that the one who said, this is my body, is the same one who said, I was hungry and you gave me no food. If Christ is present at the altar, he's also at the door. Third, the order.
What good is it, he asks, to load Christ's table with gold cups while he himself is dying of hunger?
Feed him first, he says. Then adorn his table too. Fourth, what he isn't saying.

He doesn't call beautiful churches a sin, and says plainly he isn't forbidding gifts for the altar. He's asking for the poor alongside them, and before them. Gold cups and a fed neighbor can belong together.

teach.h: NOT GOLD INSTEAD OF THE POOR.
teach.b: The danger is gold instead of the neighbor.
He later served as bishop of Constantinople, made powerful enemies there, and died in exile. The golden mouth wasn't always a safe one.

how: Catholics honor Saint John Chrysostom as a Doctor of the Church, and his words on honoring Christ in the poor are read in the Church's Office of Readings.

games.q: you're a wealthy listener. you want to honor Christ, and you have gold to give. what does Chrysostom tell you?
o: give it all to the altar.
feed the hungry first, then adorn his table.
keep it; God doesn't need it.
games.why: feed him first, he says, then decorate his table. the one who said this is my body also said I was hungry.

practice: Think of the next thing you plan to buy just to make life a little nicer, a candle, a plant for the shelf; nothing wrong with it.
Before it, picture one small gift to someone in need, a food bank, a shelter's wish list, a meal for the person outside the store, and then the nice thing after it, in its place.
If you pray, ask to see Christ in the person you give to.
